name: Cinematic film still
means: A frame lifted out of a motion picture: wide anamorphic framing, one motivated key with everything else falling away to shadow, shallow focus, and set-dressed depth behind the subject. Not a portrait - a moment inside a scene.
prose: a still frame from a feature film, anamorphic 2.39:1 framing, one motivated practical light source with deep falloff into shadow, shallow focus on the subject, set-dressed background receding into darkness, 40mm anamorphic lens with horizontal flare
negative_add: illustration, anime, cgi render, flat even lighting, stock photo, centred snapshot
works_for: video - the best-matched card in the set, since a film still is already a frame of a film and composition is what LTX preserves best. Flare and any fine grain will still crawl between frames. Inferred, not measured.
note: This card exists to stop you writing the word 'cinematic'. studio/tags/cinematic.json measured that word as close to inert: it names a quality and this box renders nouns. Everything in prose above is the concrete substitute - aspect ratio, one light source, falloff, lens. And be clear that half of what people mean by cinematic is not the style at all, it is the GRADE: blockbuster and bleach_bypass in studio/looks/ do that part deterministically after generation, every time. Reach for the look first and this style second. On the anime checkpoint the honest answer is not this card - it is camera and lighting tags plus a look. | Downgraded to untested: NOTHING in this library was rendered when it was authored, so every strength and engine call is a considered prediction. This project's own standard - written on the Illustrious checkpoint card - is that a recommendation is not a measurement.
